result.keyword: What's the best project management tool for a startup?
result.markdown:
For most startups, I'd recommend **Linear** as the best overall project management tool, particularly if you're building a tech product or running a software-focused startup.

However, the best choice depends on your team's size, working style, and whether you need to manage product development, sales, marketing, operations, or everything together.

Here's how I'd compare the leading options.

## Best project management tools for startups

![Fast growing startups are built on Linear](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/piHpddRS6n9dTggcCRU3QzspXui7xfTg4qksC0xamyVTz0l5rmZLEYCGsVB7KKUouzfiOTbe-9ydzUq7UB2MFrNbZIGlaUSNjP0C8Bhd2CXnbxL2xZ05zw3USDTcATN8Ed4Fr3ygsGaA-sAB5VFRUeF1jd3BNolTylsoZGFQvpYkliFtHTL_AgaQh3gID9Z3?purpose=fullsize)

**1\. Linear**

(Best for tech startups)

- Excellent product roadmaps and sprint planning.
- Fast, clean interface.
- Great for engineering and product teams.
- Integrates with GitHub and Slack.

Website: [Linear](https://linear.app/)

---

![Finastra Customer Story | ClickUp™](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/OXxUksa73j7hoTxbYQ6zo3pspX36GflPBLMsRWXjhfWZTJdFq6md_tXaxCCc_3Kjh0xQSrUSgXoCYi3d5TOe48r-mvzFwLplQbgf4lhsH3q_bsATt_hAcyva5qI1DtZG8OasgRxxldReZAIfURcJdNdt2Br8nPVvqn-lCO5aR2MxpFl9QAiCxibf4gzehOOb?purpose=fullsize)

**2\. ClickUp**

(Best all-rounder)

- Tasks, documents, goals and dashboards.
- Custom workflows and automations.
- Can manage almost every department.
- Good value for a growing team.

Website: [ClickUp](https://clickup.com/)

---

![How Notion’s product team brings context and clarity to work (with a template you can use)](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/lB_DgkYrcKsSrK75HhI-s1e0YZmsm9h_ko94aVDn4A57_H0BYO6jOLX7YhGfoLV-bb4yZopgv2ajtj1n2We49qlpkk2pSieb2pIRviX_-Hr7lmml6M-YGw3ewQrsNynTN4ECfMG5mdrQ4ymJ88hPWB0GVS25bKPyi-T-D3MjbFToeY3dypV9fuSvgJ-n9TsY?purpose=fullsize)

**3\. Notion**

(Best for early-stage startups)

- Combines company wiki, documents and tasks.
- Great for storing processes and meeting notes.
- Flexible enough to evolve with your business.
- Requires more setup to create sophisticated workflows.

Website: [Notion](https://www.notion.com/)

---

![How to Set Up and Use Asana Portfolios for Better Project Management | Cirface](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/H9BdGlMyDzgBrRpDEr0Ynb6h_0_rpTdSbtEo-8xN-H4AnVrpxeTDynM-6GvpGogjqdBC72dw5fWqtxa7KcvbuYINGBkUAHvdW3agU4L3JNlfBnc3rrsVTy3ycSasDQbGBGWPT5sujj-EjLp4LT1Ml71Smw4H6BNlaO1BHtrasyshgIPeIoBavxM-YcekL-tG?purpose=fullsize)

**4\. Asana**

- Excellent for cross-functional teams.
- Clear task ownership and deadlines.
- Good project timelines and dependencies.
- Particularly useful as teams grow.

Website: [Asana](https://asana.com/)

---

![How to Toggle Trello Views: Calendar, Table, Timeline & More](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/Md351UxojPqr7NcZARTUVuAl7ocTctX4xXxse2slXCoIC1a14ed7C82Suo3_BLOf8uMvPvkR6a7txy4RworeyrfELrkzyRnZeSU5JT9wx8ysI4A-zP3PbB-iwMrUJ8znrFR0rgAWlJ-HP1EFK6mtsJMgFbfykp-Rc-ETfrBKJfKEo5IF5n0UcFY7ie8JejkV?purpose=fullsize)

**5\. Trello**

- Very easy to learn.
- Excellent visual task boards.
- Minimal setup.
- Can become limiting as workflows become complex.

Website: [Trello](https://trello.com/)

These choices reflect the different strengths identified in recent 2026 comparisons. ## Quick comparison

| Tool | Best use | Complexity |
|--------|--------|--------|
| Linear | Product & engineering | Low |
| ClickUp | Whole business | Medium |
| Notion | Knowledge & planning | Low–medium |
| Asana | Team coordination | Low–medium |
| Trello | Simple task tracking | Very low |


## My recommended startup setup

If I were setting up a startup from scratch, I'd consider\:

- **ClickUp** for company-wide projects, tasks and execution.
- **Notion** for company knowledge, strategy, SOPs and documentation.
- **Slack** for day-to-day communication.

If the startup is heavily software-focused, I'd swap ClickUp for Linear for product and engineering.

The biggest mistake is adopting too many tools too early. Start with one central place for work and make sure everyone actually uses it.

## Let me narrow it down to the right choice

There are three things that would change my recommendation.

**What type of startup are you building?**

**1\. What kind of startup?**

**2\. How big is your team?**

**3\. What do you primarily want to manage?**
